coverage_note: Authority proposal for the Ras Al Khaimah Transport Authority (RAKTA). Leads with the domestic coastal spine connecting the resort islands, lagoon communities and the city corniche; a within-UAE Al Marjan↔Dubai Islands express is secondary and optional.

partner_context.their_ambition: Under the RAKTA Transport Master Plan 2030 you're standing up a marine network and connecting Al Marjan Island to the city — just as RAK becomes one of the region's fastest-growing waterfront destinations.
partner_context.their_pressure: A string of resort islands and lagoon communities is arriving fast along the coast, served today only by congested coastal road — and UAE Net Zero 2050 demands a clean fleet.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier lets you build the public water spine clean from the start — fast, near-silent foiling vessels suited to the reclaimed-island breakwaters and shallow lagoons, fitting RAK's appetite for advanced mobility.

hero.title: RAK RAKTA × Navier — a clean public water spine for the new RAK coast
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling network connecting Al Marjan Island, Al Hamra, Mina Al Arab and the city corniche — clean from the start, fit for RAK's appetite for advanced mobility.
hero.what_we_do_together: We help RAKTA stand up a clean public water network from the start — connecting the resort islands, the lagoon communities and the city corniche with fast, near-silent, zero-emission foiling vessels, ahead of the Al Marjan / Wynn demand wave.

why_now: RAKTA has opened a Marine Transport Project and is connecting Al Marjan Island to the city, just as a wave of waterfront demand arrives with Al Marjan/Wynn (opening 2027) and the Mina Al Arab and Al Hamra communities. UAE Net Zero 2050 mandates a clean fleet. Foiling lets RAK leapfrog straight to a zero-emission water spine — and fits its clear appetite for advanced, autonomous-ready mobility.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling is a step-change in comfort, speed, wake, noise, and efficiency versus conventional small craft, making marine mobility credible as a scheduled public layer rather than a novelty ride.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: The first deployments use existing waterfronts, marinas, ferry terminals, and resort arrivals; no new right-of-way or vertiport-style infrastructure is required for the proposal case.
why_navier_now.the_moment: GCC authorities are modernizing public transport while waterfront districts, resorts, and cross-border business links are growing faster than road corridors can absorb.

proof_points.claim: RAKTA has started on the water.
proof_points.evidence: The RAKTA Marine Transport Project has introduced a heritage Abra service, and Classic Taxi routes now connect Al Marjan Island with Al Qawasim Corniche.

proof_points.claim: A wave of waterfront demand is arriving.
proof_points.evidence: Al Marjan Island and Wynn Al Marjan (opening 2027), plus the Mina Al Arab and Al Hamra communities, form a coastal string served today only by road.

proof_points.claim: RAK is investing in advanced, clean mobility.
proof_points.evidence: Autonomous shuttle trials on Al Marjan Island and an eVTOL MOU with Skyports show RAK's appetite for next-generation transport.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the network model in the Maldives.

objections.concern: Is RAK's marine network ready for this?
objections.response: RAKTA has already opened a Marine Transport Project and is connecting Al Marjan to the city. Navier lets you build the public water spine clean from the start rather than retrofitting a diesel fleet later.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the optional Dubai leg uses the long-range hybrid with no offshore charging at all.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe around the reclaimed islands and lagoons?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil zones at lagoon entrances and berths, automatic speed and wake limits, and conventional low-speed handling in shared water.
